codeReview.summary: The refactor hit the size/organization targets for `App.tsx`, but it does not preserve behavior: the new shell mounts `useMuseHandlers` twice, which duplicates side effects and splits command/autopilot state away from the UI-visible muse/workspace state.

issues.description: `App.tsx` mounts `useMuseHandlers` twice (`muse` at lines 87-96 and `museWithDeps` at 119-128). Because the hook owns internal state plus a `useEffect` that drains `museEvents` via its own `processedMuseEventSeqRef` (`part64/frontend/src/hooks/useMuseHandlers.ts:152,493-541`), every incoming event is processed twice. That duplicates toasts/overlay pulses and breaks the requirement that the refactor render/behave identically to the pre-refactor app.

`useAutopilotController` and `useChatCommandHandlers` are wired to the bootstrap `muse` instance (`App.tsx:105-116`), but the UI only exposes and mutates `museWithDeps` state (`App.tsx:143-168`). `useChatCommandHandlers` calls `buildMuseSurroundingNodes(presenceId, null)` (`part64/frontend/src/app/useChatCommandHandlers.ts:148-159`), and that helper reads workspace bindings from the bootstrap hook's private state (`part64/frontend/src/hooks/useMuseHandlers.ts:317-360`). After a user changes the active muse or workspace pins, slash commands/autopilot can run against stale context instead of the selection shown in the UI.

summary: Reviewed the feature transcript, handoff, skill, shared-state docs, and commit `4c482a3`. The decomposition met the line-count/organization goals, but the bootstrap/final `useMuseHandlers` split introduces duplicate event side effects and stale command/autopilot context, so the feature does not fully preserve App behavior.
